evidence: H finite simple vertex-transitive with an edge implies 1≤a=alpha(H)≤N/2: uniform maximum-independent-set marginal a/N and a fixed-edge exclusion inequality.
Mean q=(a/N 1,0) of all maximal-cardinality independent-set vertices yields exactly Q=a-a²/N; hub h=(0,1) is distance squared D=1+a²/N from q.
λ=max(0,D−Q)/(2D), t=(1−λ)a/N; 0<t<1/2. Every rim independent-set vector of size k has squared distance Nt²+λ²+k(1−2t), so contacts occur precisely at k=a.
Hub squared distance D(1−λ)² is ≤ Q+Dλ² with equality iff δ=D−Q≥0. Exact slack for k<a is (a−k)(1−2t)>0 and screened-hub slack is −δ.
Weight all maximum rim vertices by (1−λ)/|A| and hub by λ. Their barycenter is c; the weighted squared-distance identity equals R²+||y−c||² for arbitrary y, proving global optimum and unique center.
For complement C_N (N≥5) the independent number is 2; δ=−1+8/N is zero at N=8 and negative for N≥9. This witnesses sharpness with no false finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact Euclidean invariant of the natural cone/join operation on graph stable-set polytopes. The formula gives center, radius, all support/contact classes and strict slack uniformly for infinitely many nonmultipartite vertex-transitive rims. The non-obvious feature is the exact apex price at which a newly added graph vertex ceases to alter the minimum ball, with a sharp a=2 boundary between complement cycles 8 and 9. Such exact graph-dependent data could be needed in metric graph-polytope classifications. The answer is not a known-table recomputation or arbitrary fixed-dimension slice; generic distance-variance formulas alone do not supply the graph threshold, although the independent orbit calculation is elementary.
residual_risks: The formula may be derivable as a routine exercise from established Boolean projection and symmetry lemmas; this overlap reduces claims of conceptual novelty, despite the motivated explicit classification.
No hardness/computational improvement for finding alpha(H) is claimed.

scientific_limitations: Finite simple vertex-transitive graph H with at least one edge; unweighted standard Euclidean indicator polytope, no arbitrary affine transformation.
Result conditional on alpha(H), which can be hard to compute; no asymmetric-rim or weighted norm formula.
